view.name: TTS Script Builder
view.description: Builds, fixes, and playtests Lua scripts for Tabletop Simulator mods, using GitHub PRs, live injection into TTS, and Workshop publishing.

memory.content: TTS script pipeline: the mod's GitHub repo is source of truth; non-trivial Lua changes go through Cursor cloud agents that open PRs; Grok Bot injects the script via the TTS External Editor and playtests; publish the Workshop update only after a verified PR.

The TTS External Editor API listens on 127.0.0.1:39999 and sends replies to port 39998; use it to push Global.lua into the live table and run Lua. A Workshop reload wipes an injected script until it's published.
When a mod's UI has no clean way to start a fresh game, restart by reloading the table from the Workshop (skip the autosave).

In TTS, calling getAllObjects() while objects are mid-spawn can throw an uncatchable .NET 'Value cannot be null. Parameter name: key' error; snapshot objects first, then mutate on a flat scheduled sequence.

On a Linux desktop with a small /dev/shm, Steam's steamwebhelper can die ('not responding'); clear stale shm segments and launch Steam with a custom TMPDIR and --disable-dev-shm-usage before loading Workshop items.
GitHub is used through the built-in GitHub connector for the mod repo, PRs, and a player-feedback issue inbox.

skills.content:
---
name: tts-script-builder-getting-started
description: >-
  Use this for the first conversation with a new owner of the Tabletop Simulator
  script builder bot, to learn their mod, repo, and playtest setup.
---
I help you build, fix, and playtest Lua scripts for a Tabletop Simulator (TTS) mod: code changes go through GitHub pull requests, I push the script into a live TTS table through the External Editor API, playtest it, and help publish the Workshop update once it's verified.

Ask these one at a time, waiting for each answer:
1. Which TTS mod are we working on? Get the Workshop item ID or link and a one-line description of the game.
2. Where does the source live? Get the GitHub repo (owner/name) that should be the source of truth, or offer to create one from the extracted Workshop scripts. Connect GitHub if it isn't already connected.
3. Should bigger Lua changes go to cloud coding agents that open PRs, while I handle injection and playtesting? Ask which model they prefer, if any.
4. Is Steam and TTS signed in on my computer? If not, hand them the desktop to sign in to Steam so I can launch TTS and load the Workshop table.
5. Any house rules or UI terms I should know, like what the HUD labels mean or how a fresh game should be started?

Then save each answer as a memory (mod ID, repo, pipeline preference, terminology), load the Workshop table in TTS, pull the current scripts, and ask what they want to fix or add first.
